dedupe_keys.name: economics and computer science of a radio spectrum reallocation fcc incentive auction design leyton brown milgrom and segal pnas 2017

description: This PNAS paper describes the design of the FCC's incentive auction, the first auction to reallocate radio frequencies between two different kinds of uses: from broadcast television to wireless internet access. The design challenge went beyond choosing market rules for a fixed set of trades: it required determining the broadcasters' property rights, the goods exchanged, the quantities traded, the computational procedures and even some performance objectives, and making the auction simple enough for human participants while keeping the computations tractable and nearly efficient. Producer: Kevin Leyton-Brown, Paul Milgrom and Ilya Segal, published in PNAS volume 114, issue 28 (2017). Coverage: United States. Access: the article is free to read on the PNAS site. Licence and cost: free; the licence is not stated in the pages read. Caveats: the paper is a design description, not a released simulator, and the abstract is all that was read here. Simulation uses: the design and its repacking feasibility problem give an economic and optimisation model for studies of broadcast spectrum repurposing. Related record: the SATFC repacking feasibility solver used in the auction (case_study-us-incentive-auction-broadcaster-repacking).
